questions.question: In which group of states does the Luni River flow? लूनी नदी किस राज्य समूह में बहती है?
questions.solution: The Luni River originates in the Aravalli Range near Ajmer in Rajasthan and flows southwestward into the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat. It is the largest river in the Thar Desert and is saline in its lower reaches.

• "Creative" means having original ideas or the ability to produce new concepts. The best synonym is "Innovative", which means introducing new ideas or methods.

Other options:

• (2) Likeable → Incorrect, as it means "pleasant or friendly," which is not related to creativity.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1 in the passage.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice. The concert tickets were bought by my friend.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The concert tickets were bought by my friend.

options.text: My friend has bought the concert tickets.
options.html: My friend has bought the concert tickets.

options.text: My friend bought the concert tickets.
options.html: My friend bought the concert tickets.

options.text: My friend buys the concert tickets.
options.html: My friend buys the concert tickets.

options.text: My friend is buying the concert tickets.
options.html: My friend is buying the concert tickets.

questions.solution:
• The given sentence is in passive voice (The concert tickets were bought by my friend).

• To convert to active voice, we need subject + verb + object:

o Subject: "My friend"

o Verb: "bought" (past tense of "were bought")

o Object: "the concert tickets"

Other options:

• (1) My friend has bought the concert tickets. → Incorrect, as it changes the tense to present perfect.

• (3) My friend buys the concert tickets. → Incorrect, as it changes the tense to simple present.

• (4) My friend is buying the concert tickets. → Incorrect, as it changes the tense to present continuous.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don't find any error, select 'No error' as your answer. Mr. Ali's shop / is further to / the hospital.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don't find any error, select 'No error' as your answer.

Mr. Ali's shop / is further to / the hospital.
questions.solution:
• The phrase "is further to" is incorrect. The correct preposition should be "farther from" when referring to physical distance, or "further than" when referring to degree or extent.

• Correct sentence: Mr. Ali's shop is farther from the hospital.

Other options:

• (2) No error → Incorrect, as the error exists in the preposition usage.

• (3) Mr. Ali's shop → No grammatical error here.

• (4) the hospital → Correct phrase.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It rain a lot in this part of the country.

It rain a lot in this part of the country.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She was foolish enough to think that she be completely safe now.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She was foolish enough to think that she be completely safe now.
questions.solution:
This is correct because the sentence uses past tense ("She was foolish") and requires the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact situation. The subjunctive form "were" properly completes the thought that she incorrectly believed herself to be safe.

The complete corrected sentence would read: "She was foolish enough to think that she were completely safe now."

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. all the plants and animals of today B. it is written that Brahma is the God of creation C. and it is He who has made D. in the book of Hindu mythology
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. all the plants and animals of today

B. it is written that Brahma is the God of creation

C. and it is He who has made

D. in the book of Hindu mythology
questions.solution:
The first part should introduce the subject, which is most likely about Hindu mythology and Brahma.

Part D "in the book of Hindu mythology" works as an opening phrase.

Part B "it is written that Brahma is the God of creation" naturally follows as it tells what the Hindu mythology book states.

Part C "and it is He who has made" continues the thought about what Brahma did.

Part A "all the plants and animals of today" completes the thought by stating what Brahma created.

When arranged properly, the sentence should read: "In the book of Hindu mythology, it is written that Brahma is the God of creation, and it is He who has made all the plants and animals of today."

This corresponds to option 2: DBCA
